title: PREoperative mapping of lymphatic tracts during vascular procedures and resections near inguinal and upperleg vasculature to reduce postoperative lymphatic FISTulae: The PREFIST Pilot study
summary: During surgery on the vessels and operations close to the vessels, lymphatic channels are often injured due to their proximity and their small size. This causes lymph to leak out of the lymphatic ducts and empty into the wound cavity. This can result in the inserted drains having to remain in place for a long time after an operation or, after removal of this drainage, a collection of lymph in the wound cavity (lymphocele) or even draining out of the wound suture. The consequences of such a condition are longer hospital stays, repeated operations to find and ligate the lymphatic tracts or wound infections that lead to the destruction of the vessels/plastic vascular replacement with the result of acute bleeding or blood poisoning (Sepsis).  With this study, we want to color the above-mentioned lymphatic tracts with a dye (patent blue) before the operation so that we can see them clearly during the operation and can protect them, stop them or obliterate them with the current in a targeted manner in order to reduce or avoid these complications. To do this, we mark the lymphatic channels with patent blue by injecting the dye onto the foot approximately 1 to 2 hours before the operation.
conditions: Other specified noninfective disorders of lymphatic vessels and lymph nodes

interventions.name: Subctaneous injection of Patentblau 1-2 hours preopertaively in the foot
Patients are operated traditionally without mapping of lymphatic tracts

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Elective vascular procedures of the groin und upper leg
2. Near vascular resections of the groin and upper leg
Exclusion criteria:
1. Missing declaration of consent
2. Withdrawal of the declaration of consent
